title: Electronic Commerce Transactions
outcomes: Apply registration rules for ECOs and sellers.

meta.exam_tip: First decide whether the supply is under section 9(5); if so, no TCS.

concepts.title: E-commerce operators and registration
body: An e-commerce operator (ECO) is whoever runs — by owning, operating or managing — a digital platform used for e-commerce. ECOs liable under section 9(5) or required to collect TCS must register irrespective of turnover.

Suppliers through ECOs that collect TCS must register irrespective of turnover, except (i) suppliers of services with aggregate turnover up to ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh in special States) and (ii) notified suppliers of goods meeting conditions (intra-State, PAN-linked enrolment, etc.).
Composition dealers may supply goods through ECOs under a special procedure; the ECO collects TCS and does not allow inter-State supplies by them.
concepts.analogy: Platforms and many sellers on them must register from the first rupee.
concepts.work: A home-décor seller on a marketplace must register even with ₹5 lakh sales.

concepts.title: Tax payable by ECO under section 9(5)
body: Section 9(5) makes the ECO liable for tax on notified services supplied through it: passenger transport by radio taxi, motor cab, maxi cab, motorcycle, omnibus or other motor vehicle; hotel, inn, guest house, club and campsite accommodation (with exceptions where supplier is registered); housekeeping services such as plumbing and carpentry (unless supplier is registered); and restaurant services (except from specified premises).
The ECO pays the tax as if it were the supplier and issues the invoice; the underlying suppliers need not register only because of these services.
Supplies covered by section 9(5) are excluded from TCS computation.
concepts.analogy: For notified services the platform is the taxpayer.
concepts.work: A cab aggregator pays GST on rides by unregistered drivers.

concepts.title: Tax collection at source by ECO
body: Section 52: an ECO (not being an agent) collects TCS at 0.5% (0.25% CGST + 0.25% SGST/UTGST, or 0.5% IGST) on the net taxable value of other suppliers' sales routed through its platform where it collects the consideration — gross value less returns, excluding section 9(5) supplies.
The ECO pays TCS by the 10th of the next month and files GSTR-8 by then; an annual statement is due by 31 December after the year. The supplier claims the amount in its cash ledger after acceptance.

Officers can seek details of supplies, stock and warehouses from the ECO; failure attracts penalty. Mismatches between the ECO's statement and the supplier's returns are communicated and, if not rectified, added to the supplier's liability.
concepts.analogy: Platforms withhold half a percent on net sales of sellers.
concepts.work: Net sales of ₹9 lakh through a platform carry TCS of ₹4,500.

concepts.title: OIDAR and online services from abroad
body: Online information and database access or retrieval (OIDAR) services — such as streaming, cloud services, online advertising, e-books, digital data storage and online gaming — supplied with minimal human intervention through the internet are covered by special provisions. Place of supply follows where the recipient is located.

A foreign OIDAR supplier selling to non-taxable online recipients (unregistered persons, including those registered only for TDS or Government bodies not engaged in business) in India must register under a simplified scheme and pay IGST; where an intermediary arranges the supply, the intermediary is deemed the supplier.
For supplies to registered persons in India, the recipient pays IGST under reverse charge. Online money gaming suppliers from abroad must register and pay tax regardless of OIDAR status.
concepts.analogy: Foreign digital services to Indian consumers are taxed in India.
concepts.work: A US streaming service selling to Indian households pays 18% IGST.

illustrations.title: TCS by an e-commerce operator
illustrations.q: ShopKart, an ECO in Karnataka, facilitated intra-State sales by registered sellers of ₹10,00,000 in November 2026; goods worth ₹1,00,000 were returned in the same month. It also facilitated restaurant services of ₹2,00,000 on which it pays tax under section 9(5). Compute TCS.

illustrations.title: Foreign streaming service
illustrations.q: StreamWave Inc. (USA) earns ₹50,00,000 in a quarter from subscriptions sold to unregistered individuals in India, and ₹20,00,000 from registered Indian businesses. Determine tax implications.

remember: Returns reduce net value for TCS.

viva.q: Who is a non-taxable online recipient?
viva.model: An unregistered person (including those registered only for TDS or Government bodies not in business) receiving OIDAR services in India.

viva.q: How does a supplier claim TCS?
viva.model: By accepting the amount on the portal, after which it is credited to the electronic cash ledger.

viva.q: When is an ECO not required to collect TCS?
viva.model: For supplies on which it itself pays tax under section 9(5), and for exempt supplies.

viva.q: Who pays tax if the ECO has no presence in India?
viva.model: A representative in India, or an appointed person, pays on its behalf.

viva.q: What happens to mismatches between GSTR-8 and the seller's return?
viva.model: They are communicated and, if not rectified, added to the seller's output liability.
